clue.text: It sickens mum, accepting a hundred whiskies from dictator

indicators.note: the word for mum takes the hundred in, as a host accepts a guest

parts.note: SH is the call for silence, keeping mum
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: something dictated is spoken aloud, so the whiskies are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: malts are malt whiskies

explanation.surface: A tyrant hands round whiskies to a mother who finds the whole show nauseating.
explanation.walkthrough: SH holding C gives SCH; MALTS as dictated sounds like MALTZ, which finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is cloying sentimentality, the sort of mush that turns a viewer's stomach.

clue.text: Coming together in sport at opening, Princes lift Royal Galas?

parts.note: a scrum is where rugby forwards come together

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Princes is taken

explanation.surface: Rugby princes at a match lift the trophy at a royal gala.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Gala is an apple variety, so 'lift' means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrump is to steal apples from an orchard, such as Royal Galas.

clue.text: I'm not sure virus is pretence

parts.note: hum, as in hum and haw, is a noise of hesitation
a bug is an informal word for a virus

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that a claimed virus is genuine rather than a sham.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug is hypocritical sham or deception, a false show.

clue.text: Bat Out of Hell, Dead Ringer and Bad Attitude are just routine

definitions.text: Bat Out of Hell, Dead Ringer and Bad Attitude are
definitions.meaning: these are albums by Meat Loaf, whose real name was Marvin Lee Aday
normal, nothing out of the ordinary

explanation.walkthrough: The titles look like random phrases, but they are Meat Loaf albums, and the singer was born Marvin Lee Aday.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a task that is simply part of the normal job, unremarkable.

clue.text: Specifically how craftsman's getting on after introduction to trade floor

indicators.note: the rest follows on after the opening letter
the introduction to a word is its first letter

parts.note: i.e., that is, specifies what was meant
a sailing craft's progress is measured in knots

explanation.surface: A tradesman starts work laying a floor and wants to know how it is coming along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' is a verb here, meaning to baffle; craft is a boat, whose speed is in knots.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie someone in knots is to confuse them utterly, as a baffling problem does.

clue.text: Three juxtaposed TVs will share this transmitter

indicators.note: the answer is spread across the run of three sets, which hold it between them once the outer letters fall away

parts.note: a TV is a set, so three of them side by side read SETSETSET

explanation.surface: Three television sets in a row all pick up the same broadcast transmitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Write SET three times running; the answer sits inside, from the first T to the last E, so the opening SE and closing T drop away.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly carries and passes on sleeping sickness, so it is a transmitter of disease.

clue.text: Respond to early call, perhaps hit wicket?

definitions.meaning: get up and get moving when called in the morning
in cricket a batsman is out hit wicket when he disturbs his own ...

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the stumps are the three upright posts of the wicket; read literally the phrase is knocking them.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for getting moving or bestirring yourself, as when roused early.

clue.text: Prince Myshkin, eponymously short, receives orphan girl

indicators.note: the small drink takes the girl in, receiving her

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a tot
Heidi is the orphan girl of Johanna Spyri's Swiss novel

explanation.surface: A tale about a prince who takes in a little orphan girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky's novel takes its title from its hero Prince Myshkin, the naive figure others call a fool.

clue.text: Denounce the pay scale of the MD?

parts.note: a managing director is a senior executive, an exec
a rate of pay

explanation.surface: Staff condemn the managing director's salary.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 4,4, the answer reads as the rate an exec is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or denounce something with loathing.

clue.text: Manuscript retired copper takes aboard night stage

indicators.note: the reversed policeman takes the manuscript on board, holding it inside
retired here means withdrawn, going back, so the word for copper is read backwards

parts.note: a peeler is old slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel

explanation.surface: A retired policeman's manuscript memoir covers a phase of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Peelers, named after Sir Robert Peel who founded London's police, is old British slang for police officers; 'retired' signals reading backwards, not a pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: REM sleep is the rapid-eye-movement phase of sleep, one stage of the night's cycle.

clue.text: Trim beef, maybe? A prime selection!

definitions.text: Trim beef, maybe? A prime selection!

indicators.note: keep only the letters in prime-numbered positions (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13) and drop the rest

explanation.surface: A butcher's boast: neatly trimmed beef, a prime cut chosen with care.
explanation.walkthrough: Number the letters of TRIMBEEFMAYBE; those in prime positions 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13 are R, I, B, E, Y, E. The whole clue doubles as the definition, since this steak is a prime cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribeye is a choice steak cut from the rib, a prime piece of beef.

clue.text: Contacting practice, Dr Black has rung in "poorly" — there's sad news in it

indicators.note: the practice word sits touching the rest, in contact at the end
the doctor and black hold the shuffled letters between them, as something has or contains them

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

indicators.note: poorly means unwell, out of shape, so the letters of rung in are rearranged

parts.note: order in the sense of established procedure or custom

explanation.surface: A GP named Dr Black phones in sick to the practice, and the news inside is sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr Black' looks like one person's name, but it splits into two abbreviations that hold the rearranged letters between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mourning border is the black edging on stationery once used to announce a death, so the paper carries sad tidings.

clue.text: See 11
A timeless legend duets with song and dance fan

indicators.note: the pieces pair up side by side, as in a duet
less the time, so the T for time is taken out

parts.note: a legend is a story, fiction
a song and dance is a fuss, ado

explanation.surface: A legendary star duets with someone on a song-and-dance number for a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen enthusiast or devotee of something.

clue.text: Done loudly, taken in through the nose, tobacco supply extinguished?

definitions.text: Done loudly, taken in through the nose, tobacco supply extinguished?

parts.words: Done loudly, taken in through the nose, tobacco supply extinguished?
parts.note: snuff, powdered tobacco, is sniffed noisily up the nose; when the supply has been consumed it is gone, and the phrase also means put out, like a candle

explanation.walkthrough: The parse is disputed: the blog suggests a draughts term for taking, said aloud, inside SNOUT, prison slang for tobacco, but no reading fits every word cleanly, so the clue is treated as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To be snuffed out is to be extinguished like a flame, or killed off.

clue.text: Playing surface within reach of Raiders?

definitions.meaning: a round table for the card game loo
open to being looted by raiders

explanation.walkthrough: Remove the hyphen and the card table becomes something raiders can loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Loo is an old card game played at a round table, and anything lootable can be plundered.

clue.text: Ex is someone without a yen?

definitions.meaning: ex means former, so something ... the case
a person who doesn't long, a yen being a longing

explanation.walkthrough: Yen looks like Japanese money but means a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: No longer means formerly but not now, as ex does for an ex-partner.

clue.text: See 3
What covers Iain's beginning, in original style o' Scotsman?

definitions.text: What covers Iain's beginning, in original style o' Scotsman?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the initial, covering it
rearranged in a novel way, so the letters of o' Scotsman are reworked
the first letter of Iain's is I

explanation.surface: A query about how an original Scotsman's name such as Iain is studied.
explanation.walkthrough: O'SCOTSMAN rearranged holds I; the whole clue also defines the answer, since the study covers names like Iain.
explanation.definitionFit: Onomastics is the study of proper names and their origins, which would cover a Scottish name such as Iain.

clue.text: See 6
Intended sponsorship short of one name

indicators.note: lacking, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: sponsorship is finance for a project
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A planned sponsorship deal falls short when one name pulls out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's intended is the person they are engaged to marry.

clue.text: Missing singular companion, Bigfoot ready to spring out of the Ark

definitions.text: ready to spring out of the Ark

indicators.note: the abbreviations are absent, taken out of the name

parts.note: Sasquatch is another name for Bigfoot
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Without a mate, Bigfoot is poised to leap from Noah's Ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the Ark' marks the word as antiquated; Noah's animals went in two by two, hence missing companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Asquat is an archaic word for squatting, crouched as if about to leap.

clue.text: Basic support for toddler on which infant may count …

definitions.text: Basic support for toddler on which infant may count …

parts.words: Basic support for toddler on which infant may count …
parts.note: a toddler stands on its feet, and the little digits at the base are what a child counts on in the this-little-piggy rhyme; baby talk names them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' means both rely on and literally count, as small children do with their toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby talk for feet or toes, the little supports a toddler walks on and an infant counts.

clue.text: See 22
… revealed by odd snippets from Bridget Jones, the greatest of them all

indicators.note: take the letters in odd positions, the first, third, fifth and so on, as snippets

explanation.surface: Continuing the toddler theme, a toe is found through the diary heroine Bridget Jones, the best of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the counting toes of the previous clue, so 'them all' means the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the five digits on a foot, the big one is the largest.

clue.text: Capital city is, by the way, where we are currently cycling

indicators.note: the last letter is moved round to the front, as in a cycle

parts.note: ATM is text-speak for at the moment, currently
and, as a link adding something by the way
the UK is where the setter and Telegraph readers are

explanation.surface: A traveller notes, in passing, that the capital is where they are now cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: ATMANDUK has its final K brought round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Katmandu (Kathmandu) is the capital city of Nepal.

clue.text: Find pain of old regret returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ake is an old spelling of ache
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Finding the pain of an old regret coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes' cry 'I have found it' is also used as a noun for a discovery.

clue.text: Like empty vessel lieutenant takes on short visit to Nod?

indicators.note: the lieutenant takes the nap on after himself, adding it

parts.note: a ship's first lieutenant is called Number One, written NO I

indicators.note: short means missing its final letter

parts.note: the Land of Nod is sleep, so a siesta is a brief trip there

explanation.surface: A naval officer takes a quick nap, a short trip to dreamland.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says empty vessels make the most noise, so the definition points at the loudest.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty vessels make most noise, so an empty vessel would be the loudest of all.
